edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Sed enim nationes extraneae ab omni intellectu spiritalium potestatem eadem efficacia idolis suis subministrant, sed, viduis aquis, sibi mentiuntur. Nam et sacris quibusdam per lavacrum initiantur, Isidis alicujus, aut Mithrae, ipsos etiam deos suos lavationibus efferunt. Caeterum villas, domos, templa totasque urbes aspergine circumlatae aquae expiant passim, certe ludis Apollinaribus et Eleusiniis tinguntur. Idque se in regenerationem et impunitatem perjuriorum suorum agere praesumunt. Item penes veteres quisquis se homicidio infecerat, purgatrice aqua se expiebat. Igitur si de sola natura aquis, quod propria materia sit abluendi in auspicia emundationis, blandiuntur, quanto id verius aquae praestabunt per Dei auctoritatem, a quo omnis natura earum constituta est? Si religione aquam medicari putant, quae potior religio, quam Dei vivi? quo agnito, hic quoque studium diaboli recognoscimus res Dei aemulantis, cum et ipse Baptismum in suis exercet. Quid simile? Immundus emundat, perditor liberat, damnatus absolvit. Suam videlicet operam destruet, diluens delicta quae inspirat ipse. Haec quidem in testimonium posita sunt repellentibus fidem, si minime credant rebus Dei, quarum affectationibus apud aemulum Dei credunt. Annon et alias sine ullo sacramento immundi spiritus aquis incubant, adfectantes illam in primordio divini spiritus gestationem? Sciunt opaci quique fontes, et avii quique rivi, et in balneis piscinae, et euripi in domibus vel cisternae, et putei, qui rapere dicuntur, scilicet per vim spiritus nocentis. Nam et enectos et lymphatos et hydrophobos vocant, quos aquae necaverunt, aut amentia vel formidine exercuerunt. Quorsum ista retulimus? Ne quis durius credat Angelum Dei sanctum aquis in salutem hominis temperandis adesse, cum Angelus malus profanum commercium ejusdem elementi in perniciem hominis frequentet. Angelum aquis intervenire si novum videtur, exemplum futuri praecucurrit. Piscinam Bethsaidam Angelus interveniens commovebat; observabant qui valetudinem querebantur. Nam si quis praevenerat descendere illuc, queri post lavacrum desinebat. Figura ista medicinae corporalis spiritalem medicinam canebat, ea forma, qua semper carnalia in figura spiritalium antecedunt. Proficiente itaque in hominibus gratia Dei, plus aquis et Angelo accessit: qui vitia corporis remediabant, nunc spiritum medentur: qui temporalem operabantur salutem, nunc aeternam reformant: qui unum semel anno liberabant, nunc quotidie populos conservant, deleta morte per ablutionem delictorum. Exempto scilicet reatu, eximitur et poena. Ita restituitur homo Deo ad similitudinem ejus, qui retro ad imaginem Dei fuerat; imago in effigie, similitudo in aeternitate censetur. Recipit enim illum Dei spiritum, quem tunc de afflatu ejus acceperat, sed post amiserat per delictum.
pass_a_gloss: But indeed foreign nations from every spiritual understanding supply the same efficacy to their idols, but they deceive themselves with empty waters. For they are also initiated into certain sacred rites through a bath, of some Isis or Mithra, they even carry out their own gods with washings. Moreover, they sprinkle villages, houses, temples, and entire cities with water, certainly they are drenched at the Apollinaris and Eleusinian games. And they presume that they do this for their regeneration and impunity from their perjuries. Also, among the ancients, whoever had defiled himself with homicide, expiated himself with purifying water. Therefore, if they boast about the nature of waters alone, because it is the proper material for cleansing in the auspices of purification, how much more truly will waters provide this through God's authority, by whom all their nature is established? If they think that water is healed by religion, what religion is more powerful than that of the living God? By which, having been recognized, we also recognize here the study of the devil, emulating the things of God, since he also practices Baptism among his own. What is similar? The unclean one cleanses, the destroyer liberates, the condemned one absolves. Certainly he will destroy his own work, washing away the faults which he himself inspires. These things have been put forth as a testimony to those repelling faith, if they do not believe in the things of God, whose affections they believe among the emulator of God. Do they not also at other times, without any sacrament, incubate unclean spirits in waters, affecting that primordial gestation of the divine Spirit? All know the dark springs, and the bird-haunted streams, and the pools in the baths, and the channels in the houses or cisterns, and the wells, which are said to be seized, certainly by the force of the harmful spirit. For they call those who have been drowned, and those who are frenzied, and those who are hydrophobic, whom the waters have killed, or have exercised with madness or fear. Why have we recounted these things? So that no one may more harshly believe that the holy Angel of God is present in the waters, tempering them for the salvation of man, when the evil Angel frequently frequents the profane commerce of the same element for the destruction of man. If the intervention of the Angel in the waters seems new, it anticipates a future example. The Angel intervening moved the pool of Bethsaida; those who sought health observed it. For if anyone had preceded others in descending there, he ceased to complain after the bath. This figure of bodily medicine sang of spiritual medicine, in the form in which carnal things always precede spiritual things in figure. Therefore, with the grace of God profiting in men, more has been added to the waters and the Angel: who remedied the vices of the body, now heal the spirit; who operated temporal salvation, now reform eternal salvation; who once a year liberated one person, now daily preserve the people, death having been deleted through the washing away of faults. Certainly, with the guilt removed, the penalty is also removed. Thus man is restored to God in His likeness, who before was in the image of God; the image is considered in the likeness, the likeness in eternity. For he receives the Spirit of God, which he had then received from His breath, but afterwards lost through fault.

to convey the idea of making amends or atonement
to convey the idea of spiritual rebirth

pass_b_english: Foreign nations, devoid of any spiritual understanding, ascribe the same power to their idols, but they delude themselves with empty water. They even undergo initiation through a bath—dedicated to some Isis or Mithras—and they actually wash their own gods. Moreover, they sprinkle villages, houses, temples, and entire cities with water; at the Apollinarian and Eleusinian games they drench themselves thoroughly. They presume this earns them rebirth and immunity from their perjuries. Among the ancients, anyone who had defiled himself with homicide would expiate his guilt with purifying water. So if they boast of water's natural property alone—claiming it is the proper material for cleansing in the rites of purification—how much more truly will water deliver that power through God's authority, since He established its very nature? If they think religion sanctifies water, what religion surpasses that of the living God? Once that is acknowledged, we recognize here the devil's mimicry, aping the works of God, because he too practices a baptism among his followers. What a resemblance: the unclean one cleanses, the destroyer liberates, the condemned one absolves. He will inevitably wreck his own work, washing away the very sins he inspires. These facts stand as testimony for those who reject the faith: if they refuse to believe the things of God, why do they credit their counterfeits in the devil's camp? Do not unclean spirits also, without any sacrament, brood over waters at other times, mimicking that primordial brooding of the divine Spirit? Everyone knows the dark springs, the remote streams, the pools in baths, the channels in houses or cisterns, and the wells said to be seized—surely by the force of a harmful spirit. They call the drowned, the frenzied, and the hydrophobic—those whom waters have killed or driven to madness and terror. Why recount all this? So that no one may find it harder to believe the holy Angel of God attends the waters to temper them for human salvation, when the evil angel habitually exploits the profane use of the same element for human destruction. If an angel's intervention in water seems novel, it anticipated a future pattern. An angel descending stirred the pool of Bethesda; those seeking healing watched for it. Whoever managed to step in first ceased his suffering after the washing (John 5:4). That figure of bodily cure foreshadowed spiritual cure, following the rule that carnal realities always prefigure spiritual ones. As God's grace advanced among humanity, something greater was added to the water and the angel: they once healed bodily ailments, now they heal the spirit; they once procured temporal safety, now they remake eternal salvation; they once freed a single person once a year, now they preserve multitudes daily, death having been abolished through the washing away of sins. With guilt removed, punishment is also removed. Thus man is restored to God in His likeness—he who was originally made in God's image; the image lies in the likeness, the likeness in eternity. For he receives the Spirit of God, which he first received from God's breath but later lost through sin.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A is a faithful literal gloss, and Pass B is a fluent translation that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between 'imago' and 'similitudo'. The scripture citation (John 5:4) added in Pass B is a correct identification of the allusion to the pool of Bethesda. All clauses, including the complex descriptions of demonic activity in waters and the theological conclusion regarding the restoration of the image/likeness, are present in both.
